responses.reason: Fair point, S8 spends a lot of words on a $1,600 line while bigger accounts barely get a sentence.
I noticed this too, S2 says 28,200 but the table shows $229,000 moved, so it grabbed the percent instead of the dollar figure.
S6 does say those invoices arrived after close and get booked in July, so that reads like a real cutoff timing issue.
Professional fees only moved $7,500, under the $25,000 commentary threshold stated up top, so a driver was not actually required here.
Same thing I flagged, S5 says the program finished June 30 and S9 says repairs are still finishing in August, which cannot both be true.
I did not redo the math myself, but if it does not hold up unrounded then the stable margin line should not stand as written.
I caught this one too, S7 says bad debt increased $42,000 but the table shows $47,000 moved on that line.
Warehouse wages moved $72,500 and is starred in the table, so it should have gotten a driver and it just does not have one.
Matches what I saw, S4 calls it a decline but the table shows inbound freight rose $73,800, so the direction is backwards.
I cannot rule that out myself, so if a transfer is sitting inside that revenue number it should be pulled out before calling it organic growth.
Flat depreciation while the memo talks about depot work does seem worth asking about, even though I have not seen the asset detail.
S3 just asserts the Tri-State driver without showing depot-level numbers, so I agree we would need that split before taking it as given.
